blocks.h2: When It's Time to Replace Your Water Heater
blocks.intro: Replacement is the right call when repairs stop making sense. Here's how to tell:

tiles.body: Once the tank itself corrodes through, it can't be repaired. Shut off the water to the heater and call.
Tank heaters typically last about 8 to 12 years. An older heater that needs a major repair is usually a replacement.
If your household has grown or you've added a bathroom, the heater may simply be too small. Replacement is a chance to size it right.
When one repair follows another, the money is usually better spent on a new heater.

blocks.intro: A new water heater touches your gas or electric supply, your venting and your water lines. Here's how we handle each part:

steps.body: We look at your household, your bathrooms and your current setup to recommend the right capacity and fuel type, tank or tankless.
You get a flat-rate price for the heater and the install before any work begins.
We remove the old heater and install the new one with the venting, gas or electric and water connections today's code requires.
We test for leaks and proper operation, walk you through the new heater and leave the work area clean.

blocks.h2: Installing Water Heaters in Highland Park Homes
blocks.intro: Nearly half of Highland Park homes were built before 1960, and about 1 in 4 before 1940. Older homes bring a few things to plan for.

items.body: Older chimneys, vents and gas lines weren't always built for today's heaters. We check them before the install, so there are no surprises on the day.

Older basements can have tight stairs, low ceilings and small utility rooms. We plan the swap around your space, and we'll tell you if a different size or a [tankless unit](/highland-park/tankless-water-heater) fits better.
Colder incoming water in a Lake County winter means the heater has to work harder. We size your new heater for the season it'll struggle most in, not just the average day.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton
blocks.intro: Price shock is the most common complaint about water heater replacement. Here's how we avoid it.

steps.body: We diagnose the heater before we recommend anything. If a part fixes it, that's what we'll tell you.
We walk you through both options, what each costs and how long each is likely to last, so the decision is yours.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Installation Questions From Highland Park Homeowners

items.q: How long does it take to replace a water heater?
items.preview: A straight tank swap usually takes a few hours. Bigger changes take longer.
items.answer: A straight swap of a tank heater usually takes a few hours. Moving the heater, changing fuel type or switching to tankless can take longer. We'll give you a realistic timeline before we start.

items.q: Can a handyman legally replace a water heater in Illinois?
items.preview: It should be done by a licensed plumber. Gas, venting and plumbing all have to meet code.
items.answer: Water heater replacement involves gas or electric connections, venting and plumbing, and it should be done by a licensed plumber and permitted where required. An improper install can create a carbon monoxide or water damage risk that doesn't show up right away.

items.q: What size water heater do I need?
items.preview: It depends on your household and bathrooms. We size it for how you actually use hot water.
items.answer: It depends on how many people live in the home, how many bathrooms you have and when you use the most hot water. We'll look at your household and recommend a size, not just replace what you had.

items.q: How much does it cost to replace a water heater in Highland Park?
items.preview: It depends on the heater and any code updates. You get a flat price first, with financing available.
items.answer: It depends on the heater type, capacity and fuel, plus any venting, gas or code updates your setup needs. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins. Financing is available so you can get it done now and pay over time.
